children: Indian equity markets extended their rally for a fourth consecutive session on Tuesday, with the benchmark indices rising more than 1.5 per cent, supported by strong corporate earnings, a recent decline in crude oil prices and signs of renewed buying by foreign portfolio investors.

The Nifty 50 gained 1.58 per cent to close at 23,810.85, while the BSE Sensex advanced 1.62 per cent to 76,917.85. Both indices have risen around 5 per cent over the past four sessions and ended at their highest levels in two months.

The gains came despite subdued trading across several Asian markets, where technology stocks declined ahead of voting in the US midterm elections. Indian equities appeared to attract investors seeking exposure beyond the global artificial intelligence-led technology trade.
Market breadth was largely positive, with 13 of the 16 major sectoral indices closing higher. The Nifty Midcap 100 rose 1.1 per cent, while the Nifty Smallcap 100 gained 0.3 per cent.

Financial stocks and private sector banks were among the biggest contributors to the benchmark indices' advance. The financial services index rose 1.8 per cent, while the private banking index gained 2 per cent.
HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank, which together account for nearly a fifth of the Nifty 50's weight, climbed 3.6 per cent and 2.7 per cent, respectively.
Among stocks outside the benchmark indices, Marico gained 10 per cent after reporting quarterly profit above market estimates.

Foreign portfolio investors have been net buyers in four of the past five trading sessions, according to the data cited in the report. Expectations of a possible long-term capital gains tax cut, along with steady corporate earnings, have supported investor sentiment.

Crude oil prices remain an important factor for the domestic market. Brent crude rose around 1 per cent to USD 106 a barrel on Tuesday, after falling 7 per cent in the previous session. Investors were assessing developments involving talks between Iran and Qatari mediators, as well as reports of a US attack on Iran's Qeshm island.
Higher crude prices can add to India's import costs and inflationary pressures, making movements in the oil market an important consideration for investors.
The sustainability of the market rally will therefore depend on corporate earnings, foreign investment flows and developments in global energy markets.
